response.content:
## AI Companies That Entered the Norwegian Market in 2026

Norway has seen significant activity from AI-related companies in 2026, primarily driven by demand for AI data center infrastructure. Here are the key entrants and expansions:

### Major AI Infrastructure Players

- **Nscale** (UK-based neocloud) — Already operating an AI data center in Glomfjord, Norway (powered by 30 MW of hydroelectric power), Nscale expanded significantly in 2026. In April 2026, it announced a further 30,000 Nvidia Rubin GPUs for a new 230 MW data center in Narvik (Kvandal), northern Norway, developed under a joint venture with Norwegian energy company Aker ASA. Microsoft is the anchor tenant for this site, with a $6.2 billion deal for computing power. The Narvik facility is currently under construction.

- **Microsoft** — Deepened its Norwegian presence in 2026 by contracting major AI computing capacity from Nscale at the Narvik data center. Microsoft stepped in as the primary customer after OpenAI dropped out of the "Stargate Norway" project.

- **Cerebras** — The AI chip company (an Nvidia rival) signed contracts for additional data center capacity in Norway and Finland in 2026, with new facilities in Norway expected to begin operating in the coming months. More than 75% of Cerebras's data center capacity coming online in 2027 will be located outside the US, with Norway among the key locations.

- **atNorth** — The colocation provider expanded into Norway in 2026 by purchasing land for a planned mega data center in Haugaland, initially delivering 120 MW and scaling to 350 MW at full capacity (slated for 2028).

- **TikTok / ByteDance** — Operates a 150 MW "Project Clover" EU data center in Hamar, Norway, which became operational as part of its European data sovereignty efforts.

### Broader Context

The influx of AI companies into Norway has been so intense that in November 2026, the Norwegian government and grid operator Statnett announced a temporary halt on new data center grid connection reservations (until at least August 2027). Energy Minister Terje Aasland noted that Statnett had received connection applications for 26,000 MW of new capacity in 2026 alone — more than Norway's entire current peak consumption — with data centers accounting for 75% of requests. Digitalization Minister Torgeir Micaelsen stated: *"We want data centers in Norway, but we can't have all types of data centers."*

A Norwegian Board of Technology report found that foreign companies own 90% of data centers in the country, and that these facilities create few lasting jobs after construction.

Norway also established an AI partnership with the United Kingdom on 12 November 2026, aimed at cooperation on AI safety, research, and infrastructure.
